record.original_question: Determine whether particle trajectories of Euler flows are analytic in time in arbitrary dimension, and how that analyticity depends on the presence and analyticity of boundaries. This includes clarifying the status of Yudovich-class trajectories, which are known to be Gevrey regular but not known to be analytic.

evidence.quote: Problem 12. Are particle trajectories analytic in time in any dimension? For fluids on manifolds with boundary how does this analyticity depends on whether the boundary is analytic or not? Nadirashvili [113] proved analyticity of flow lines of a stationary solution to the 2D Euler equation. His theorem is local and holds independently of the analyticity (or the lack thereof) of the boundary ∂M . It follows the classical analyticity proof for solutions of analytic elliptic equations and uses the fact that an elliptic equation becomes hyperbolic if one of the variables, say x1 , is replaced by ix1 . (It is worth recalling that flow lines and vorticity lines coincide for stationary 2D solutions and hence are analytic simultaneously.) Remark 6.2. In dimensions d = 2 and 3 the analyticity of particle trajectories in Rd (i.e. in the case without boundary) was proved in [26]. Apparently the higher dimensional case does not present fundamentally new difficulties, and the study in [26] was confined to low dimensions because of their physical significance. The paper [55] covers several related cases, including vortex patches among other situations. There is also the following related problem: Are particle trajectories of Yudovich solutions analytic in time? (Recall that the Yudovich class consists of divergence-free vector fields u sat- isfying kcurl ukL∞ < ∞. This inequality implies that the field u has the Osgood property [117], which guarantees the uniqueness of trajectories.) It is currently only known that they are Gevrey regular, due to the result in [50], see also [23]. It seems to be unknown if this Gevrey regularity is sharp.1 The difficulty here is as follows. It is known that Sobolev vector fields are integrated to Sobolev diffeomorphisms; in other words, Sobolev vector fields form the Lie algebra of the group of Sobolev diffeomorphisms. However, it is unknown what would be the result of integration for vector fields from the Yudovich class, i.e. what are “Yudovich homeomorphisms”. Do such homeomorphisms form a group? Does this “group” admit the structure of a real Banach manifold? Can this “manifold” be complexified? Presumably, the answers are “no” to all those questions, and one has to look for other approaches to this problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the incompressible Euler equations
  ∂_t u + (u·∇)u = -∇p,   div u = 0,
on a smooth Riemannian manifold M (possibly with boundary ∂M), with the no-penetration condition u·ν = 0 on ∂M. Given a sufficiently regular initial velocity u_0, let X(t,x) denote the Lagrangian flow map defined by
  d/dt X(t,x) = u(t, X(t,x)),   X(0,x) = x.

(a) Determine whether, in every spatial dimension d ≥ 2, the particle trajectories t ↦ X(t,x) are real-analytic functions of time on their interval of existence, for the case M = ℝ^d (no boundary).

(b) For fluids on a manifold M with boundary, determine how the time-analyticity of particle trajectories depends on the regularity of ∂M: in particular, whether analyticity of trajectories holds when ∂M is merely smooth (non-analytic) versus when ∂M is real-analytic.

(c) In the Yudovich class on a two-dimensional bounded domain (initial vorticity ω_0 ∈ L^∞ giving rise to a unique global weak solution with a continuous flow), it is known that particle trajectories are Gevrey regular in time, with the Gevrey order depending on the regularity of the boundary. Decide whether such Yudovich-class trajectories are in fact real-analytic in time.
artifact.status_search_result: Time-analyticity of Lagrangian particle trajectories is established in ℝ^d for d = 2, 3 (Serfati, Shnirelman, Frisch–Zheligovsky and follow-ups), and is generally believed to extend to higher dimensions without fundamentally new difficulties, but a complete published treatment for all d and for general boundary cases is not standard. For Yudovich solutions in bounded 2D domains, results establish Gevrey regularity of trajectories (with Gevrey order depending on boundary regularity) but full real-analyticity in the Yudovich class remains unresolved. Thus the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.snippet: Problem 12. Are particle trajectories analytic in time in any dimension? For fluids on manifolds with boundary how does this analyticity depend on whether the boundary is analytic or not?
status_evidence.claim: The problem is stated as open in this open-problems compilation.

status_evidence.title: On the Analyticity of Particle Trajectories in the Ideal Incompressible Fluid (Shnirelman)
status_evidence.snippet: Particle trajectories of ideal incompressible fluid are analytic curves, even though solutions of the Euler equations may have finite regularity.
status_evidence.claim: Analyticity established in low dimensions without boundary.

status_evidence.title: Time-analyticity of Lagrangian particle trajectories in ideal fluid flow
status_evidence.snippet: Ideal flow with limited spatial smoothness has time-analytic Lagrangian trajectories.
status_evidence.claim: Time-analyticity proved via Cauchy's Lagrangian formulation.

status_evidence.title: On the analyticity of the trajectories of the particles in the patch problem for 2D Euler
status_evidence.snippet: Analyticity of trajectories for vortex patches in 2D Euler.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results for vortex patches; general Yudovich class not covered.

status_evidence.title: On the analyticity and Gevrey class regularity up to the boundary for the Euler Equations
status_evidence.snippet: Gevrey regularity of trajectories for bounded vorticity in domains with Gevrey boundary.
status_evidence.claim: Yudovich trajectories are Gevrey, with order tied to boundary regularity; full analyticity not established.
